events.title: Strait of Hormuz could reopen as part of Qatari plan for Iran nuclear inspections
events.summary:
Trump still considering new assault on Iran nuclear sites – though threats less credible after Vance remarks

Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors to visit Iran’s bombed nuclear sites, including those housing the country’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

Iran would not be required to make any commitment that the stockpile would be removed from the country, with other options on the table, including reducing the uranium content by down-blending it.

Continue reading...

events.title: US midterm results may help unite Israeli coalition to unseat Netanyahu
events.summary:
Democrats’ sweep could urge Israel’s divided opposition to join forces and remove prime minister closely allied with Trump

The Democrats’ sweep of Congress may make it easier for Israel’s splintered opposition to overcome deep internal divisions and form a coalition government, by increasing the urgency of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu, who has associated himself so closely with Donald Trump’s Republicans.

But as Israel took stock of the results, there was also a sense that the elections marked a longer-term shift in US politics that will make the job of any new Israeli leader far more difficult.

Continue reading...

events.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm
events.summary:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo

The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.

Continue reading...

events.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’
events.summary:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

  • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.

Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

Continue reading...

events.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying
events.summary:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.

This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.

Continue reading...

events.title: Tens of thousands protest against Narendra Modi regime in Delhi
events.summary:
Led by Congress party, India’s opposition alliance channels anger over removal of 130 million names from voter roll

Thousands of opposition supporters have gathered in Delhi as protests against the Narendra Modi government continue to gather momentum.

Led by the Congress party, India’s opposition alliance has brought together supporters from across the country, amid growing anger over a large-scale revision of the country’s voter roll that has seen 130 million names erased.

Continue reading...

events.title: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India
events.summary:
Rubio’s decision not to meet Narendra Modi last week was seen by some as a snub – but by focusing on business leaders and oil, the secretary of state made American priorities clear. Plus: the artist bringing a female perspective to men’s clothing

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went.

The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.

Continue reading...

events.title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons
events.summary:
‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show

Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years.

The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.

Continue reading...

events.title: Teaching GCSE topics younger risks turning schools into ‘early exam factories’, Powell warns
events.summary:
Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum

Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education.

Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.

Continue reading...

events.title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS
events.summary:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.

As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

Continue reading...

events.title: Russell Brand case must be wake-up call to protect women in media, Lisa Nandy says
events.summary:
Culture secretary says there is still a problem with exploitation and abuse in the industry and public life

The culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, has said there is still a problem with exploitation and abuse in the media industry and a failure to properly deal with allegations after Russell Brand’s conviction for rape and sexual assault.

She said women who came forward were too often not protected by institutions across public life, including in politics, and that huge power imbalances meant speaking up came at a very heavy cost.

Continue reading...

events.title: Riot breaks out at influencer boxing event attended by Tommy Robinson in Ireland
events.summary:
Two people arrested after Robinson’s presence inflames tensions in scenes witnessed by many on social media

Two people were arrested at an influencer boxing event that descended into a riot in Ireland after the presence of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson inflamed tensions in the crowd.

The riot took place at about midnight on Saturday at an event organised by the controversial internet personality HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, at the Hub events venue in Kilkenny.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary
events.summary:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters

Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).

Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms
events.summary:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says

The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women.

On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT.

Continue reading...

events.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore
events.summary:
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident

A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California, fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.

The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.

Continue reading...

events.title: Small plane crashes into pickup truck on busy Florida highway
events.summary:
No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard

A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was injured in the dramatic incident.

Video footage obtained from the sheriff’s office shows a Cessna 172 grazing over the truck as it approached the ground for a complete landing on a road in Fort Meyers at about 11.45am on Saturday.

Continue reading...

events.title: Hakeem Jeffries supports impeachment of Pete Hegseth: ‘He has got to go’
events.summary:
House Democrat is a ‘hard yes’ on impeachment resolution against defense secretary who ‘has abused his power’

House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become majority leader, said on Sunday that he strongly supports impeaching defense secretary Pete Hegseth as a Republican lawmaker prepares to force a House vote.

The top Democrat made his position clear during an appearance on ABC’s This Week, declaring himself a “hard yes” on the impeachment resolution targeting Hegseth.

Continue reading...

events.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
events.summary: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.

events.title: Trying to find true owners, Paris' Musee D'Orsay exhibits art looted by Nazis
events.summary: A new permanent exhibition at Paris' Musee d'Orsay showcases works of art suspected to have been looted by Nazis during the Second World War in France. Experts are trying to find the true owners or their descendants.

events.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
events.summary: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.

events.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
events.summary: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

events.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
events.summary: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.

events.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

events.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
events.summary: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.

events.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
events.summary: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

events.title: A correspondent finds Cuba's people struggling
events.summary: Reporting from Cuba comes with distinct challenges especially amid widespread power outages and fuel shortages.

events.title: Israel's president taps opposition candidate, not Netanyahu, to form a government
events.summary: Gadi Eisenkot ran as the main rival to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but neither won enough support to command a majority. Israel's main parties have recommended Eisenkot form a new government.

events.title: Pope Leo urges Argentina's Milei to put people before the economy
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV has urged Argentina to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor, delivering a message to President Javier Milei over austerity, social welfare and political divisions.

events.title: Nvidia CEO Huang admits affair amid rumors of China spy ties
events.summary: Following reports of Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang becoming involved with a Chinese spy, Huang offered an apology for cheating on his wife. Meanwhile, the US tech company pledged to investigate the alleged espionage.

events.title: Iran: Trump says strikes unlikely if peace talks keep moving
events.summary: After weeks of rumors that the US and Israel were preparing new strikes on Iran, President Donald Trump said it was "highly unlikely" that he would order a new escalation as the Iranians "want to make a deal so badly."

events.title: Germany news: Merz to nominate Aigner for president
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

events.title: Many killed after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
events.summary: The incident occurred near Kebemer off the coast of northwestern Senegal. Authorities on El Hierro in the Canary Islands have declared an emergency after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.

events.title: South Africa elections: ANC marks its worst-ever performance
events.summary: The African National Congress, the party of late Nobel Prize winner Nelson Mandela, slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. The voters blame the ANC for water and electricity shortages.

events.title: Egypt train crash leaves several dead, over 100 injured
events.summary: A train derailed after colliding with another train south of Cairo, with authorities confirming several deaths and saying more than 100 passengers were injured. Over 50 ambulances were deployed to the scene.

events.title: Israel: Eisenkot officially tasked with forming a government
events.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with the right of trying to form a government. The opposition leader's way to replacing Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister is full of political challenges.

events.title: Iran: US strikes ship after Hormuz blockade breach
events.summary: The US military said a vessel trying to leave an Iranian port was hit due to the naval blockade on the country. On its part, Iran said three "non compliant" oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Gaza: Rains add misery to humanitarian catastrophe
events.summary: With most homes damaged or destroyed by the war, Gazans are facing worsening humanitarian conditions due to heavy rain.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: Poland begins two days of mourning over Krakow shooting
events.summary: Polish authorities have opened a terror probe after the shooting on Krakow's Main Square. Police confirmed that the bodies found at the suspect's home were those of his parents and sister.

events.title: India: Delhi chokes on most polluted Diwali eve in 10 years
events.summary: Delhi was ranked as the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali. Delhi's air pollution is expected to get worse in the coming days.

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
events.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

events.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square, police say
events.summary: A suspect who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the man was fascinated with "radical" and "far-right" ideologies.

events.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
events.summary: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

events.title: Israeli president tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
events.summary: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government. Tricky coalition talks are expected.

events.title: Trump offers White House press secretary role to Dana White
events.summary: US President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the invitation.

events.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
events.summary: Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

events.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
events.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

events.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
events.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

events.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
events.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

events.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
events.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

events.title: Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
events.summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
events.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
events.summary: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

events.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
events.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
events.summary: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

events.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
events.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

events.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
events.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

events.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
events.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
events.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
events.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

events.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
events.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

events.title: Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
events.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
events.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
events.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

events.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
events.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

events.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

events.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
events.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

events.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
events.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

events.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
events.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

events.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
events.summary: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

events.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
events.summary: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

events.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
events.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

events.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
events.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

events.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
events.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

events.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
events.summary: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

events.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
events.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

events.title: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
events.summary: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

events.title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
events.summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
events.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

events.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
events.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

events.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
events.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

events.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
events.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

events.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
events.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
events.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

events.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
events.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

events.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
events.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

events.title: Germany seeks new head of state
events.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new president is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

events.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
events.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

events.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
events.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

events.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
events.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

events.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
events.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

events.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
events.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

events.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
events.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

events.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
events.summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

events.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
events.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

events.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
events.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

events.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
events.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

events.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
events.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

events.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
events.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

events.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
events.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

events.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
events.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

events.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
events.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

events.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
events.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

events.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
events.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

events.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
events.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

events.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
events.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

events.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
events.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

events.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
events.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

events.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
events.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

events.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
events.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

events.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
events.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

events.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
events.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

events.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
events.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

events.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
events.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

events.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
events.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

events.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
events.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

events.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
events.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

events.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
events.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

events.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
events.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

events.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
events.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

events.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
events.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

events.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
events.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

events.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
events.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

events.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
events.summary: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

events.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
events.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

events.title: Trump vows comeback as parties clash over Democrat prosecution threats
events.summary: President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday after Republicans lost control of Congress in last Tuesday’s midterms, as incoming Democratic leaders pledged to hold his administration to account, and the attorney general promised to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.

events.title: Nvidia to probe reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
events.summary: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.

events.title: Pope Leo criticises Milei’s austerity in Argentina, says growth must benefit all
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his tour began, facing calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei. The visit to Buenos Aires is the first by a pontiff to the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades.

events.title: Pope Leo in Latin America: Papal Politics and Peru
events.summary: Pope Leo heads to Argentina for the second leg of his South America tour, where he's expected to draw the biggest turnout of his Papacy so far. The pontiff has wrapped up his first visit to Uruguay. Colleen Dulle, Vatican Correspondent at America Magazine and the co-host of the 'Inside the Vatican' podcast, joins us to analyse the significance of his Latin American tour.

events.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot begins the hard work of forging a coalition government
events.summary: Israel's ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot was tapped by President Isaac Herzog to try to form a government Sunday evening. But his lack of a clear majority in parliament will make trying to forge a coalition alongside the country's divided minor parties an uphill struggle.

events.title: Pope Leo in Latin America: Papal Politics and Peru
events.summary: Pope Leo heads to Argentina for the second leg of his South America tour, where he's expected to draw the biggest turnout of his Papacy so far. The pontiff has wrapped up his first visit to Uruguay. Colleen Dulle, Vatican Correspondent at America Magazine and the co-host of the 'Inside the Vatican' podcast, joins us to analyse the significance of his Latin America trip.

events.title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities say
events.summary: A boat carrying migrants along the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off the coast of Senegal, killed at least 34 people, authorities said Sunday. Only one survivor has so far been found, and "an indeterminate number" are still missing.

events.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands without power
events.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday following Russian airstrikes targeting the country's energy infrastructure. Moscow has intensified its attacks as winter approaches, leaving residents in Kyiv and other parts of the country struggling with power cuts as temperatures continue to drop. Clemence Waller reports.

events.title: Gadi Eisenkot receives mandate to form government
events.summary: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has officially been tasked with forming the country's next government, following a formal announcement by President Isaac Herzog. He now has up to six weeks to negotiate with potential coalition partners and secure a parliamentary majority. While an alliance with Arab Israeli parties appears to be the easiest option mathematically, it remains politically sensitive. Eisenkot must now navigate difficult negotiations to build a coalition capable of replacing Benjamin Netanyahu. Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

events.title: Spain's Alcaraz beats error-prone Shelton to win Paris Masters for first time
events.summary: Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to American player Ben Shelton in the US Open in September as he inched ahead of his rival Sunday to win the Paris Masters for the first time. It was Shelton's first defeat in a Masters final.

events.title: The week in pictures: US midterms 'Blue Wave', French protests and Dakar Youth Olympics
events.summary: From the Democratic Party's big wins in the US midterm elections to France's ongoing student-led protests and the first Olympic sports event held on African soil, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.

events.title: US voters reject AI data centres: could the backlash spread to France?
events.summary: In Tuesday’s US midterm elections, voters weighed in on more than 40 local measures on data centres, and sided against them in all but one. With Democrats taking control of Congress in January and new governors in Texas and Georgia calling for moratoriums, the AI building boom faces its toughest political test yet.

events.title: Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsens
events.summary: One month into the Yemeni government's offensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, fighting continues to escalate along the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the humanitarian crisis is worsening, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced and the country facing the threat of catastrophe. Rula Amin, Senior Communications Advisor and spokesperson at UNHCR at Amman, in Jordan, shares further details.

events.title: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting
events.summary: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.

events.title: French skipper wins Route du Rhum
events.summary: French sailor Tom Laperche has won the Route du Rhum, setting a new record in the transatlantic yacht race. The 29-year-old crossed the finish line in Guadeloupe on his first attempt, beating the previous 2022 record by around six hours. A remarkable debut in one of sailing's toughest competitions!

events.title: Mourning in Poland after mass shooting
events.summary: Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 16 injured. The 24-year-old Polish suspect was reportedly fascinated by far-right ideologies. Authorities are investigating the possible extremist motive as Krakow's main square remains sealed. Two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.

events.title: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French FM says
events.summary: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.

events.title: Pope Leo urges men to respect wives amid Latin American femicide crisis
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV urged men to respect their wives as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America. The region recorded nearly 20,000 instances of women being killed over the past five years alone, most of them murdered by a current or former partner.

events.title: ‘10 times more painful’: Menstrual disorders fuel calls to ban tear gas at French protests
events.summary: French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests that have roiled France in recent weeks, sometimes causing grievous injuries. Thousands of accounts of women experiencing acutely painful periods and increased bleeding are further challenging assumptions that the chemical irritant carries only minor consequences.

events.title: 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games: Golden Double for Senegal
events.summary: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.

events.title: Diwali: Over one billion people mark victory of light over darkness
events.summary: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the deity celebrated during the festival, festivities included performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.

events.title: Paraguay: Senate impeached Peña rather than accept his offer to resign
events.summary: Paraguay's ousted president, Santiago Peña, has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Initially placed under house arrest, he has since been transferred to a military facility for his own safety. Nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts after regulators seized control of the online bank. Repayments are now under way, but protests continue as customers demand access to their money. Peña denies any wrongdoing. Jack Pownall reports.

events.title: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government
events.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 27 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.

events.title: Donald Trump wants UFC fighters as assistants
events.summary: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.

events.title: AI giant Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with 'Chinese spy'
events.summary: Tech giant Nvidia is investigating reports that chief executive Jensen ⁠Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

events.title: Briton among six killed by 'far-right' gunman in Krakow rampage
events.summary: A 32-year-old British man is among six people killed in a mass shooting in Krakow, in which another Briton was wounded, Polish officials have said.

events.title: Trump 'only kidding' about offering UFC boss press secretary job
events.summary: Donald Trump has said he was "only kidding" about UFC boss Dana White becoming White House press secretary.

events.summary: At least seven people have died and more than 100 have been left injured in a major train crash south of Cairo, according to the Egyptian Chief Prosecutor’s office.

events.summary: One person has died after being hit by a Ukrainian drone attack in western Russia, while Moscow has struck emergency workers on rescue missions.

Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive

events.summary: Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to support its escalating conflict with rebels in neighboring Yemen

events.summary: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, have marched through Amsterdam, demanding the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over Gaza

events.summary: At least 21 people died after a boat carrying migrants sank off Senegal's coast, according to the country's interior ministry

events.summary: Egypt's railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance.

events.summary: Tourists and locals alike witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 wounded

events.summary: Saudi Arabia has intercepted missiles targeting its capital and other regions

events.summary: Pope Leo XIV has wrapped up his visit to Uruguay by marking an important Catholic feast day tied to the country’s independence

events.summary: Croatian police say that at least two people were killed and several were injured when a bus overturned on a highway

events.summary: Poland is in mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15

events.summary: He's accused of running under the direction of China’s Communist Party.

events.summary: New Zealanders face weeks of uncertainty after Saturday's election, with no clear winner emerging

events.summary: A strong earthquake with a preliminary reading of magnitude 5.7 has struck central Japan

events.summary: A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia killed three soldiers and injured at least 8, Colombia’s army said

events.summary: Paraguay's former President Santiago Peña has been taken to the attorney general’s office for questioning

events.summary: Pope Leo XIV has urged an estimated 40,000 people in Uruguay to build bridges of fraternity and faith

events.title: Airstrike kills at least 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
events.summary: Airstrikes in a town near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, have killed 22 people and wounded 30 others, mostly women and children, according to a spokesman for Yemen’s Houthi-run Health Ministry

events.title: Iran says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges, and other Mideast news
events.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard has lifted its self-imposed limit on the range of its ballistic missiles, hinting at potential developments for longer-range capabilities

events.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says his personal data has been leaked on the dark web, exposing him to threats and intimidation

events.title: What to know about the hoax bomb threats that targeted flights in Europe
events.summary: Dozens of flights across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats this week, causing diversions and emergency landings

events.title: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom
events.summary: On his way to school in Vienna on the morning of 10 November 1938, eight-year-old Arthur Schneier watched his synagogue burn while firefighters and police officers stood by “rejoicing”.

events.title: ‘For the first time I have my own chair’: Gaza siblings find new freedom
events.summary: In Gaza, 10-year-old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each of their hands. They struggle to move around and perform daily activities like eating and writing independently.

events.title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
events.summary: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

events.title: World News in Brief: Civilians killed in DR Congo, Ukrainians wrestle with return, Guterres calls out ‘normalisation’ of force
events.summary: At least 30 civilians were killed overnight on Thursday in Beni Territory, North Kivu in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to local sources cited by the UN aid coordination office (OCHA).

events.title: From a ship frozen into Arctic ice, a warning to world leaders: Trust the science
events.summary: Drifting through the polar darkness, a team of scientists is documenting a rapidly changing Arctic. As sea ice retreats and oil tankers move in, a conversation with the UN chief reveals why the battle for climate science matters far beyond the North Pole.

events.title: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues
events.summary: Aid teams working to help millions of people uprooted by the ongoing war in Sudan appealed on Friday for more international assistance amid desperate funding shortages, empty warehouses and overwhelming needs.

events.title: ‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis
events.summary: The climate emergency is an immediate crisis for refugees, with three in four – nearly 90 million people – living in countries facing high to severe exposure to hazards such as drought, floods and extreme heat.

events.title: World News in Brief: Korea tensions mount, UN demands answers over staff death in Yemen, Guterres in Spain, Nepal alert ahead of COP31
events.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres remains concerned over the situation on the Korean Peninsula, including the potential escalation of tensions across the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), his Spokesperson said on Thursday.

events.title: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
events.summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

events.title: Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple
events.summary: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children’s risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

events.title: Two new Ebola vaccines to join DR Congo clinical trial
events.summary: Two new Ebola vaccine candidates will be added to a clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as the country continues to battle a deadly outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.

events.title: COP31 explained: What’s at stake at this year’s UN climate summit?
events.summary: The world has more tools than ever to tackle climate change, yet millions remain unable to benefit from them. As clean energy technologies advance faster than ever, the challenge facing countries at COP31 is no longer just finding solutions – but making sure everyone can afford them.

events.title: UN peacekeeping chief warns of ‘security vacuum’ as Blue Helmets leave Lebanon and Western Sahara
events.summary: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara risks leaving a dangerous security vacuum, while the Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

events.title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
events.summary: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

events.title: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
events.summary: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.

events.title: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
events.summary: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

events.title: 15 years of ‘almost no progress’ in getting young people moving: WHO
events.summary: One in four adolescents worldwide reported not getting at least 60 minutes of physical activity on any day in the previous week, according to new global estimates released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday.

events.title: Afghan children face narrowing path to education, UN agencies report
events.summary: More than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school remain outside formal learning and millions of girls can only dream of going to university.

events.title: ‘The world is not ready’: Climate adaptation cash falls far short as warming heads past 1.5°C
events.summary: Although global warming is set to exceed 1.5°C, financing to help communities adapt to climate change falls far short of needs, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said in a report published on Wednesday.

events.title: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
events.summary: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.

events.title: World News in Brief: Children killed in Myanmar strike, new violence flares in Mozambique, an Internet affordability milestone
events.summary: A school in Myanmar has been hit in an airstrike, with three children reported killed and five others injured, according to UN Children’s Fund UNICEF.

events.title: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
events.summary: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

events.title: Gender equality pays off for business – so why are companies pulling back?
